name: Sound maker
markdown:
# Sound maker

> From the author's earlier studio, cleaned for publication: private paths, ports and some lines were removed, so a step may read short and a screen it names may not exist here. Status in this studio: Untested.


## What it makes
| You want | Engine | GPU | Always works |
|---|---|---|---|
| Any noise / effect: hits, risers, whooshes, UI, cartoon, glitch, ambience, ASMR-style textures, notes | **synth** (78 numpy sounds, `sound_maker_synth.py`) | no | yes |
| Any sound from a description | **sfx** = a backend per layer through the studio's own generate path: Stable Audio 3 small / medium (`sfx:sa3`,  a local port, 2.5-6 GB, the default), **MMAudio** (`sfx:mmaudio`, own venv, 44.1 kHz, CC-BY-NC weights) or **HunyuanVideo-Foley** (`sfx:foley_hy`,  a local port, territory-limited licence); the last two are recipe level, 2026-10-17, see [video-foley.md](video-foley.md) | yes | an unavailable backend is replaced by the next available one with a note, then the nearest synth sound |
| A voice meme: a short phrase through a studio voice, then robot / megaphone / hard-tune / chipmunk ... | **voice** = the studio TTS (Qwen3 Ryan / Aiden, a designed library voice, a character's saved preset or designed voice) + the looks | yes | **no** (there is no CPU speech synth on the box); it says the TTS is not available |
| Re-make your own audio | **sample**: cut, slice, reverse, stretch, pitch, loop, chop, stutter on a library song / studio result / upload, provenance recorded | no | yes |

## How to use it
1. Open **🔊 Sound maker**. Pick a tab: Noises & effects, Meme sounds, Trend-ready song / hook.
2. Either press a **ready-made starter** (54 of them: fail sting, riser into a drop, notification ping, awkward-silence crickets, record scratch, deadpan voice line ...), or **describe it in a sentence** and press **Write the recipe** (the local writer LLM; if it is down or wrong, a keyword planner makes a plain recipe and the page says so), or build it by hand: layers (synth / generated / voice / your audio), a **look** (40 presets with sliders: telephone, megaphone, underwater, tape stop, slowed + reverb, glitch, hard-tune, blown-out ...), loudness, loop, stereo.
3. **Make N takes** (1-6). Take A is the recipe as written, B..F vary every parameter more and use another seed. Each take is a CPU studio job; a generated or spoken layer first goes through the normal studio generate queue.
4. Play each take, open its **checklist**, then **Keep** (saves into the song library, so it shows in every song picker, with its recipe and provenance), **Drop** (deletes the file) or **+ Another take**.
5. **Your sounds** lists kept sounds with wav / mp3 export, a pack (zip with a manifest, `PROVENANCE.csv` and a licence note) and **Use in a video**.
6. **In the spirit of a trending sound** (reads the 🔥 Trending entry and, if you fetched it, measures your own copy locally): shows what the research says made that kind of sound work, each line tagged, and offers up to six original recipes that change one thing about it. Nothing is copied.
7. **Check a file** runs the checklist on any song in your library.
8. **Cut a hook out of one of your songs** (the research plan's step 2): picks a downbeat in the loudest stretch with the song library's own `pick_segment`, starts at once (no fade-in; Music 3 renders start 8-19 dB under their median), loops with a crossfade and masters to -14 LUFS / -1 dBTP (Music 3 renders peak up to +0.3 dBTP). Your song is not changed. Load it into the recipe, make the takes, keep one. It is re-made from your audio, so it carries the sample provenance and stays out of packs unless included.

## The safety rules (always on)
- The master **always** runs last: it trims silent edges, makes click-free edges, optionally crossfades a loop, brings the sound to the loudness target (-23 / -18 / -16 / -14 / -12 LUFS; **nothing above -9 is accepted**) and a look-ahead limiter holds the **true peak at or under -1 dBTP** (never above -0.5). "Blown-out (loud meme)" and "bass boosted" are still limited. A short hit that cannot reach its target without more than 6 dB of limiting stops short and says so.
- Typed text goes through the studio text guard (`character_policy.prompt_problems`). Voices: studio presets / designed voices only, **never a clone and never a real person** (`voice_options.text_problem`, `tts_preset_tools.likeness_problem`). A generated-sound prompt **never names an artist, a track or a meme sound**: a named meme sound is replaced by a plain description ("a deep resonant boom with a long sub tail"), "sounds like ..." / "in the style of ..." is refused, a song's artist is refused.
- No copyrighted audio is shipped or downloaded. The sample engine works only on audio the author already has; a pack leaves sample-based sounds out unless included on purpose. Licensing is the author's legal team's call.
- Runs are CPU jobs (`engine soundmaker`, CPU lane). A run never starts GPU work by itself; after a restart a live run becomes **interrupted** and waits for **Resume**.

## The checklist: a craft checklist, not a prediction
Going viral is mostly unpredictable (social influence, timing, who posts it, the video around the sound; best published audio-only hit prediction is about 0.74 accuracy and weak for new artists). So the score says so in the UI, the API and the code (`sound_maker_fit.DISCLAIMER`). Every check carries a **basis**:
- **EVIDENCE-BACKED**: a published result supports the *direction*; the number is still a hypothesis. Hook timing (H2), roughness 30-150 Hz for alarms and screams (H7), tempo 100-135 BPM (H12), medium syncopation (H13), steady pitch inside syllables for speech-to-song (H14: median pitch slope, 33 st/s midpoint of 27.6 vs 40), repeated wording (H15), generator-fingerprint spikes (H17, detection only).
- **HYPOTHESIS**: a starting value with nothing published for this class: length bands per class (H1), attack under 10 ms (H4), decay to -30 dB (H5), spectral shape and phone-speaker content (H6), bandwidth (H18), loop seam (H10, H19).
- **DELIVERY QC**: platform and file rules, not virality drivers: loudness near the target, true peak, clipping, dead air at the start, silent tail, DC offset, mono fold-down.
The scorer only **advises**: it never refuses a take, an export or a pack (the research synthesis recommends advise-only until it is calibrated). The score is the share of applicable checks passed (a warning counts half). It also reports a delivery score and a class score separately. The loop-seam check is slope-aware (extrapolates the last samples and compares with how far the same predictor misses inside the clip), because a raw sample difference breaks on low-frequency sounds. The checks depend on numpy only; nothing uses the removed streaming audio-features API.

## Routes (`/api/studio/soundmaker/*`)

## Hooks for other work (all three DONE 2026-10-17, author: "lets do all of this")
- **Sound cues**: `sound_cues.available()` now also offers the sounds KEPT here (`sound_cues.maker_entries(songs)` = `sound_maker_library.cue_entries`; the entry id is the library song id). They go through the same writer digest, `validate()` and ffmpeg mix as a fetched Trending noise, with the song's provenance and licence note in the report and `used_in` recorded. A song hook, a sound over 12 s, an archived sound, a missing file and a take that was never kept are skipped; `option()` and `request()` accept a kept maker id and refuse anything else. Tests: `tests/studio/test_sound_maker_cues.py`.
- **Song pickers**: a sound made here shows a 🔊 in front of its title in every picker (`songLabel` in `song_helpers.js` and `content_helpers.js`; 🔥 still wins for a trending sound). Kept sounds are in the song library (`extractor soundmaker`, `tags ["soundmaker", kind]`).
- Use in a video: the **Use in a video** button opens the Video page where a result card's Song picker lists the sound.

## Time and VRAM
Synth, looks, master, checklist: CPU, about 0.1-3 s per sound. Generated sounds: SA3 small 0.2-0.6 s warm (2.5 GiB), medium (5.7 GiB), both queued and VRAM-checked by the studio. Voice phrases: the TTS job (Qwen3 presets ~ a few GiB, FireRedTTS3 ~15.5 GB). Nothing is held between takes. **Write the recipe** calls the same local writer LLM as the shot writers (`gamebuilder.llm.chat_json`, which may load it through the normal content-model gate); it is a click, never automatic.

## Listen list: what the author should listen to (nothing below has been heard)
Run `python3 scripts/sound_maker_proof.py plan`, then (when approved) `run --approved` for the CPU sheet and `run --approved --gpu --session <id>` for the studio cases. It writes wav files, `results.jsonl` and `listen.md` to `a local folder`.
1. **78 synth sounds** at defaults (`cpu/synth/`): does each sound like its name; any click, harsh buzz or nonsense? Priority: boom, thud, slam, stab, womp, bonk, boing, whoosh, riser, drop, scratch, ping, success, laser, crickets, rain, drone, heartbeat, footsteps, typing, brush, hook_sketch.
2. **40 looks x 2 sources** (`cpu/looks/`): telephone, megaphone, walkie, underwater, behind_wall, vinyl, cassette, lofi, eight_bit, chipmunk, deep_monster, robot, ghost, hard_tune (the roughest: pitch snapping), slowed_reverb, sped_up, tape_stop, reverse_in, stutter_hit, glitched, pump, blown_out and bass_boosted (loud but never painful).
3. **Starters** (`cpu/starters/`): would you use each on a real video cut?
4. **Takes A/B/C** of 5 sounds (`cpu/takes/`): different enough, same idea.
5. **Generated sounds** (`gpu/sfx/`, 6 prompts x small / medium) and **voice phrases through the looks** (`gpu/voice/`, 6 phrases): clear speech, effect reads as intended, clearly not a real person.
6. **The checklist itself**: judge 30-50 of your own favourite and least favourite short sounds with `Check a file`, then compare the ranking with your ears; that is the only calibration there is. Re-check monthly (year-to-year drift is documented).

## Honest limits
- The synth sounds are computed from maths. Some will sound thin or toy-like next to a recorded sample; the SFX model and the sample engine are the answer for realism, and nobody has judged either.
- The pitch tools are rough: phase-vocoder pitch shift smears sharp hits, formant shift and the "hard-tune" snap are approximations, not studio tools.
- No CPU voice: voice memes depend on the TTS being up.
- The writer's recipes are validated but their taste is unproven; the keyword planner is plain word matching.
- The checklist cannot see context (the video, the cut, the caption), culture, timing or who posts it.
- Survey queue: Q1 (MMAudio) and Q2 (HunyuanVideo-Foley text-to-audio) are DONE, wired by another agent as the `sfx:mmaudio` and `sfx:foley_hy` studio entries and selectable as the backend of a generated-sound layer (recipe level, nobody has listened; MMAudio weights are non-commercial, Foley's licence is territory-limited). Q3 (DBS-BSRNN stem split) and Q4 (a CPU speech synth) are still queued.

## author decisions (settled 2026-10-17, "lets do all of this")
1. Sound cues and the 🔊 marker: both done (above).
2. HunyuanVideo-Foley and MMAudio: wired as generated-sound backends (see the engines table).
3. The loud ceiling stays: nothing above -9 LUFS and the true peak at or under -1 dBTP, "blown-out" included.
4. Packs keep leaving out sounds re-made from the author's own audio unless ticked.
Still open: calibrating the checklist against the author's ears (rate 30-50 sounds), and whether to queue Q3 / Q4.
